title_en: A Brother and Sister Make Up
note_en: 着 after a verb describes an ongoing state rather than a finished action: 写着“我错了，别生气啦” "it said, 'I was wrong, don't be mad'" — literally "was written-and-stays-written." Compare 两个人配合着打了几局 "the two of us played a few rounds, working together": 配合着 sets the background for the main verb 打. English uses "-ing" or a simple past for both, so 着 has no single equivalent.
